transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-16
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Kaur (Redwood SE), Sam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Evan Hart (LumaGuard), Maya Chen (LumaGuard), Carlos Ruiz (LumaGuard Security), Aisha Bello (LumaGuard DS), Omar Nadir (LumaGuard CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, short):
Redwood gave a migration workshop focused on mapping OpenAI/Anthropic/Together usage to Redwood API equivalents. Covered API mapping, streaming vs chunked embeddings, cost/latency tradeoffs, dedicated vs private options. Action items captured to run microbenchmarks and share parity checklist.

Topics:
- Parity mapping for generation / chat / function calling
- Embeddings dims and replacement (vector store considerations)
- Streaming, KV cache and batching implications for latency/p99
- Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private (network/KMS concerns)
- Cost modeling and Redwood Optimize suggestions

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're gonna run through a pragmatic strategy for swapping your endpoints over to the Redwood API, not just a like theory talk but a checklist and microbenchmarks you can run. sound good?
[00:18] Evan: yup sounds good. quick ask, we want parity with our Anthropic and OpenAI models — for both quality and latency. also embedd— embeddings, we use 1536 dims currently with anthro's thing so need to see mapping.
[00:32] Priya: cool, we'll show the mapping patterns. two quick q's before we start, what are your main constraints — cost, latency, or compliance?
[00:45] Maya: all three, but latency p50 and p95 matter most for interactive features; cost matters for batch embeddings. compliance is a blocker for some PII workloads — Carlos will go into that.
[00:57] Carlos: yeah for anything customer-identifiable we need VPC or Private deployment, KMS integration and audit logs. SOC 2 is table stakes.
[01:10] Jordan: totally, yep. Redwood supports hosted API for quick start, dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and a Private VPC option for network isolation. We'll point out the gaps where you might need a private install.
[01:25] Sam: small note — we sometimes see function-calling semantics differ between Anthropic and OpenAI, and Together has slightly different tokenization behavior which affects stop sequences, so parity is often about mapping behavior not one-to-one model options.
[01:40] Aisha: can you expand on tokenization differences? we've seen hidden tokens inflate costs unexpectedly.
[01:50] Priya: absolutely. Together models we saw split punctuation differently, so prompt prefixing and few-shot examples behave slightly different. on the checklist we include a tokenized sample diff: run both model tokenizers and compare token counts per prompt. that will quickly show cost variance.
[02:10] Evan: ok makes sense.
[02:15] Jordan: we'll jump into the console — quick share, 1st slide is parity checklist link: https://redwood.app/deck/lumaguard-onramp (shared in chat).
[02:28] [screen share noise]
[02:35] Priya: here in the API mapping table — left column is OpenAI/Anthropic/Together endpoint, middle is behavioral notes, right column is Redwood API call pattern. e.g. function calling: OpenAI's functions map to Redwood "tools" call with structured output. streaming works same but our streaming chunk sizes are configurable so you can tune for p50 latency.
[02:58] Maya: is there a drop-in for streaming clients? we use a custom SSE consumer.
[03:05] Priya: yes you can use our streaming protocols, we have an SSE and websocket option — small differences in chunk framing but library binds are available. we published an example in the node sdk.
[03:18] Evan: how about embeddings? we have a batch job generating 10M vectors/month at 1536 dim via OpenAI. latency for batch is fine but the cost is high. what are the redwood options?
[03:31] Jordan: Redwood supports a curated set of open embeddings and also recommend quantized variants. you'll get similar vector dims where possible; if your vector dims change we can do similarity mapping in the vectorstore adapter layer. Also Optimize will suggest quantization and caching for frequently-seen documents.
[03:50] Aisha: so if we move to a different embedding model with 1024 dims, our index will need reindexing?
[03:57] Priya: yes reindex is recommended; or you can hybridize—store old vectors and new in a single index with meta tags, but you'll see recall variance. We'll include reindexing cost estimate in the spreadsheet.
[04:12] Omar: about private deployment — our security team requires KMS/HSM integration and full audit log retention for one year. is that available?
[04:22] Sam: yes Private offers KMS integration, HSM in on-prem packs, and configurable retention for audit logs. for hosted we provide encrypted-at-rest and managed key options. we'll flag the gaps in the security doc.
[04:38] Carlos: network diagram — we need peering with our VPC, no public egress for model inputs. can Redwood support that?
[04:47] Priya: Private can run within your VPC with customer-managed egress. For Dedicated we can provide a peered connector but it depends on the cloud region. We'll request your network diagram (action item).
[05:02] Evan: the big question is cost vs latency tradeoff — we push for p95 sub-300ms on 512 token prompts, is that realistic?
[05:12] Jordan: depends on model and warm KV cache. On dedicated N5-ish instances we've seen p95 ~200-300ms for small autoregressive variants at 512 tokens. For larger models or cold cache p95 will be higher. We recommend warm sharding and continuous batching settings in the Optimize tool.
[05:35] Aisha: any quant numbers? rough cost per 1k tokens?
[05:40] Jordan: we'll give ballpark in the pricing doc; depends on quantization and batching — ballpark: $0.6-1.8 per 1k tokens depending on model/quant. exact numbers after bench.
[05:55] [crosstalk]
[06:00] Priya: let me demo a microbenchmark — i have a sample prompt pair: a chat flow (20-120 tokens) and a long generation (~600 tokens). i'll show OpenAI vs Redwood mappings and a quick latency run.
[06:15] [keyboard sounds]
[06:25] Priya: ok launching test 1, note this was run with a local microbench harness and not final production routing — this is illustrative. test 1: OpenAI gpt-3.5 like prompt -> latency 120ms p50, p95 320ms; Redwood variant on dedicated-ish config p50 110ms p95 290ms. token counts similar after tokenizer align step.
[06:50] Evan: nice. how reproducible is that?
[06:54] Priya: medium reproducibility in a lab; in your workload we'll want to run the exact prompt set through the harness — i'll run that for you as an action item.
[07:05] Maya: what's the expected engineering effort to switch endpoints? we have a microservice calling OpenAI endpoints with function calls and streaming.
[07:13] Sam: typically the SDK swap is minimal — endpoints and some param names change, function calling maps to our tool schema. The heavy work is in QA around tokenization differences and reindexing embeddings. We estimate 2-4 engineer-weeks for an initial pilot to switch a single service end-to-end including QA.
[07:33] Omar: ok that's reasonable. any gotchas with together models specifically?
[07:39] Priya: Together often uses different EOS behaviors and sometimes different stop token semantics. We include an automated stop-token compatibility check in the parity checklist.
[07:50] Carlos: SSO and RBAC — how do we provision seats and restrict by project?
[07:57] Jordan: Console supports SAML/SSO provisioning plus RBAC roles; you can sync groups and restrict model access per project. We'll include the SAML metadata doc.
[08:10] Aisha: how about fallback routing if a model is unavailable? we run multi-model routing for SLAs.
[08:18] Priya: Redwood supports policy-based routing — you can set primary/ secondary models by latency tiers, and automatic fallback to cheaper variants. We also have region fallback to keep apps online.
[08:30] Evan: show us how Optimize recommends batching — we have bursty traffic and avg 30rps but spikes to 500 for short periods.
[08:40] Sam: Optimize analyzes token distribution and suggests batch sizes and cache TTLs. for bursty loads we recommend a burst pool on Dedicated or enabling autoscale with burst capacity. The console has a histogram UI. I'll demo.
[08:55] [screen sounds]
[09:05] Sam: here is an example Optimize suggestion: for a 95th percentile token length of 120, it recommends batch size 8, KV cache TTL 10m for user context, and prefix caching for repeated system instructions — projected 18% cost drop.
[09:25] Maya: nice. can Optimize plug into our prometheus or datadog?
[09:30] Priya: yes we push metrics to your observability endpoint and supply tracing hooks; we also export token-level cost reports you can ingest.
[09:38] Evan: ok we will need traceback to link bad responses to a prompt set — is there tracing?
[09:44] Jordan: yes we have request-level tracing with optional payload hashing to avoid storing PII; audit logs include request IDs so you can trace.
[09:54] Aisha: in the demo you mentioned function/tool calling — what about structured outputs for our downstream parsers?
[10:00] Priya: Redwood supports JSON schema enforcement and structured outputs with pointers to tools; we can fall back to plain text if parsing fails. We'll include examples in the shared repo.
[10:12] Evan: earlier you mentioned the tokenized sample diffs — how do we run that?
[10:16] Priya: we provide a small script that runs your prompts through both tokenizers and outputs token counts and a diff file. We'll attach that script.
[10:24] Maya: about embeddings batching — our pipeline creates 10k vectors per job — is streaming embed creation supported?
[10:31] Sam: we support batch embeddings and streaming creation; streaming reduces memory overhead and we can checkpoint partial results to your store. For big jobs we recommend Dedicated with throughput guarantees.
[10:42] Carlos: legal asked about data retention and purge APIs. do you expose a deletion API?
[10:48] Jordan: yes deletion endpoints and data ledger for audit; for Private you control retention. For hosted, deletion requests are processed within SLA and we provide an erase token. We'll share the privacy/retention doc.
[10:58] Evan: what about cost predictability? we don't want surprise unit costs.
[11:03] Priya: you can use Dedicated reserved pool — monthly commit — to smooth unit costs and a burn-down view in console. Also we have cost alerts per token thresholds.
[11:15] Aisha: can we pilot with a single service and keep the rest on OpenAI until we're confident?
[11:20] Jordan: yes hybrid is common — route subset of traffic to Redwood using canary policy in our console, you can split traffic by user or route and observe metrics.
[11:30] Omar: timeline wise, if we sign pilot what's realistic?
[11:33] Jordan: once prompts and logs are shared, we can run microbench and demo in 1 week, pilot (single service) in 2–4 weeks depending on infra and security gating.
[11:45] [long pause, typing]
[12:00] Priya: quick note on model variants — when OpenAI has gpt-4o like variants, we map to Redwood-curated high-quality variants and also recommend quantized versions for Dedicated. We'll list recommended parameters per workload.
[12:15] Evan: can you call out what breaks parity more often — is it tokenizer, top-p sampling defaults, or streaming?
[12:23] Priya: biggest is tokenizer differences and stop token semantics, second is temperature/randomness defaults; sampling can be tuned but sometimes samples change relative ordering on re-rolls.
[12:35] Carlos: security review next steps? we'll need a deep dive with infra and legal.
[12:39] Jordan: yes we'll schedule a security deep-dive — please send your timezone availability and we will pull the security team.
[12:47] Aisha: last thing — embeddings recall drift after reindex. do you have evaluation tooling?
[12:53] Sam: yes we have eval harness to run recall/precision tests and tie regressions to prompt sets; Redwood Optimize flags regressions on a baseline.
[13:05] Jordan: ok wrapping up — recap of action items and owners in chat. we'll send the parity mapping sheet, the bench harness, pricing tiers, and security docs. any final q's?
[13:18] Evan: none here, great session.
[13:21] Omar: thanks everyone.
[13:24] Jordan: great, talk soon.

End of transcript.
